The e-text wording should be checked against the printed edition.

paraphrase: Thesis of the shorter Sanskrit recension, by the six marks: (1) opening and closing: it opens with Avalokiteśvara looking and seeing the five aggregates as empty of own-being (s3) and closes with the mantra (s9) and the colophon (s10); (2) repetition: the identity of form and emptiness said of the four other aggregates (s4-s5), and the long series of "no ..." (s6-s7); (3) novelty: form is emptiness and emptiness form, and in emptiness there is no aggregate, sense-base, realm, link, truth, knowledge or attainment (s4-s7); (4) stated result: fearlessness, going beyond inversions, nirvāṇa, the buddhas' unsurpassed awakening (s8), and the mantra as allayer of all suffering (s9); (5) praise: the epithets of the mantra (s9); (6) reasoned demonstration: the "therefore" (tasmāt) of s6 from the mark of emptiness to the negations, the "because" (cittāvaraṇa-nāstitvāt) of s8 from the unobscured mind to fearlessness, and the "therefore" of s9 introducing the praise of the mantra. The thesis: the five aggregates are empty of own-being and all dharmas are marked by emptiness, unarisen and unceased, so that in emptiness none of the listed categories is found, neither knowledge nor attainment; whoever relies on the perfection of wisdom is unobscured in mind, fearless, beyond inversions, with nirvāṇa as the end, and the buddhas awaken through it.
notes: Thesis by the extractor from the six marks (P8); it is limited to what the e-text states. Differences from the Chinese T251 are noted at s3, s7 and s8.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
